entry.name: Ansible Google Groups
entry.description: Ansible's mailing list and forum!
entry.line: - [Ansible Google Groups](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/ansible-project) - Ansible's mailing list and forum!

evidence.observation: Group header says: 'The Ansible Google Groups has migrated to forum.ansible.com.' The pinned post by Gundalow Barker (9/17/24) says: 'The Ansible Google Groups are now readonly.'

Official migration plan: new posts move to the forum, then the Google group goes read-only and all support is handled on the forum. A follow-up on 2024-09-17 by the Ansible Community Engineering Manager confirms the groups are read-only.
The Ansible Community forum (Discourse) is live, with Get Help, Project Discussions, Events and News categories and thousands of topics.
Official docs name the Forum as 'our default communication platform'.

limitations: Entry 66 (IRC) also points users to the Forum/Matrix. The maintainer may want to avoid listing the forum twice.
assessment.newDescription: The official Ansible community forum, which replaced the now read-only Ansible Google Groups mailing lists.
assessment.reason: Ansible's own announcement says the Ansible Google Groups (including ansible-project) were made read-only on 2024-09-17, and that all support moved to the Ansible Forum at forum.ansible.com. The group's banner now says it has migrated to forum.ansible.com. The listed link is now an archive, not Ansible's mailing list and forum, so the documented official successor is the Ansible Forum.

limitations: The project now calls itself "enterprise-grade" where the entry says "carrier-grade". This is marketing wording rather than a demonstrably false claim; the maintainer may optionally adopt the official wording.

assessment.reason: github.com/afourmy/eNMS redirects to github.com/eNMS-automation/eNMS, which the GitHub metadata in the packet snapshot confirms as the canonical repository (not archived, default branch "public"). The project still offers network visualization (geographical view, network builder) and workflow-based network automation, so the description stays accurate. Only the URL changes; the name stays eNMS.

entry.name: NSoT
entry.description: Network Source of Truth (NSoT) is a source of truth database and repository for tracking inventory and metadata of network entities to ease management and automation of network infrastructure.
entry.line: - [NSoT](https://github.com/dropbox/nsot) - Network Source of Truth (NSoT) is a source of truth database and repository for tracking inventory and metadata of network entities to ease management and automation of network infrastructure.

blockers: The dropbox/nsot repository has no notice pointing to the jathanism fork. The succession evidence comes from the PyPI nsot project metadata and the fork's own README, so the maintainer should confirm they accept this as an official successor rather than an independent fork.

evidence.observation: No archive banner. Description: "Network Source of Truth is an open source IPAM and network inventory database".
Text matches the entry description. Points to nsot.readthedocs.io and pynsot, with IRC on freenode. Contains no successor notice.
Latest version 2.14.2, uploaded 2026-03-27. project_urls Homepage and Repository are https://github.com/jathanism/nsot. Releases 2.11.0 to 2.14.2 date from Feb to Mar 2026.
Repository description: "Network Source of Truth - Fork of Dropbox's original NSoT that has been updated for Python 3 and Django 5.x". Default branch is main.
"NSoT was originally created at Dropbox and is now maintained by Jathan McCollum." v2.0.0 notes: Django 5.2, DRF 3.16, Python 3.10+. Install with pip install nsot.

limitations: I could not check commit history through the GitHub API (rate-limited).
assessment.newDescription: Network Source of Truth (NSoT) is a source of truth database and repository for tracking inventory and metadata of network entities to ease management and automation of network infrastructure.
assessment.reason: dropbox/nsot is not archived, and its README matches the entry description verbatim. However, the official PyPI "nsot" project (2.11.0 to 2.14.2, released Feb to Mar 2026) now lists https://github.com/jathanism/nsot as its homepage and repository. That repository's README says "NSoT was originally created at Dropbox and is now maintained by Jathan McCollum" and describes Python 3.10+ / Django 5.2 releases. Its description of NSoT is identical to the entry. The package's own distribution metadata points to it as the maintained continuation, so a replacement URL is suggested, pending maintainer review.

entry.name: ciscoconfparse
entry.description: Parse, Audit, Query, Build, and Modify Cisco IOS-style configurations.
entry.line: - [ciscoconfparse](https://github.com/mpenning/ciscoconfparse) - Parse, Audit, Query, Build, and Modify Cisco IOS-style configurations.

evidence.observation: "This repository has been archived by the owner on Mar 2, 2025. It is now read-only."

"Important: ciscoconfparse2 — ciscoconfparse is End of Life. As of December 14, 2023 ciscoconfparse2 is released; this is equivalent to version 2.0 of ciscoconfparse... You should upgrade." It warns that some legacy APIs are deprecated.
"ciscoconfparse2 is the next generation of ciscoconfparse, which was the primary development package from 2007 until 2023." It handles multi-vendor configs (Arista, Cisco, F5, Juniper, Palo Alto).
Version 0.9.18, uploaded 2026-05-17. Summary: "Parse, Audit, Query, Build, and Modify Cisco IOS-style and JunOS-style configs". Repository: https://github.com/mpenning/ciscoconfparse2.

limitations: ciscoconfparse2 is not a fully drop-in API replacement; the original README says to test code before migrating. The archived v1 repository and PyPI package (1.9.52) remain available for legacy users. I found no evidence about whether v1 receives any maintenance, and none should be inferred.
assessment.newDescription: Parse, Audit, Query, Build, and Modify Cisco IOS-style and JunOS-style configurations. Successor to ciscoconfparse.
assessment.reason: The listed repository is archived (Mar 2, 2025). Its README states "ciscoconfparse is End of Life" and that ciscoconfparse2, released December 14, 2023, is the equivalent of version 2.0 and "You should upgrade". This is an officially documented successor by the same author. ciscoconfparse2 is active (PyPI 0.9.18, 2026-05-17) and still parses, audits, queries, builds and modifies IOS-style (and now multi-vendor) configurations.

entry.description: FreeZTP is an open-source Zero-Touch Provisioning system for Cisco IOS campus switches and routers.
entry.line: - [FreeZTP](https://github.com/PackeTsar/freeztp) - FreeZTP is an open-source Zero-Touch Provisioning system for Cisco IOS campus switches and routers.

blockers: The README not mentioning routers is not affirmative evidence that routers are unsupported. The maintainer may prefer to keep the original wording if router support is confirmed elsewhere, for example in issues or wiki pages I did not check.

evidence.observation: No redirect, no archive banner. Description: "An Open-Source Zero-Touch Provisioning System for Cisco IOS." Default branch is latest.

"A Zero-Touch Provisioning system built for Cisco Catalyst switches." "FreeZTP is a dynamic TFTP server built to automatically configure Cisco Catalyst switches upon first boot... using the 'AutoInstall' feature built into Cisco IOS." The README never mentions routers. Documented version is v1.5.1.

limitations: I did not run the software. Cisco IOS AutoInstall exists on some routers as well, so router use may work in practice.
assessment.newDescription: FreeZTP is an open-source Zero-Touch Provisioning system for Cisco IOS (Catalyst) switches.
assessment.reason: PackeTsar/freeztp is canonical and not archived. Its README (v1.5.1) describes "A Zero-Touch Provisioning system built for Cisco Catalyst switches" using IOS AutoInstall, and the repository description says "for Cisco IOS". The README does not mention routers. The entry's "campus switches and routers" claim therefore isn't supported by the official docs, so a narrower wording is suggested.

entry.name: QEMU
entry.description: QEMU is a generic and open source machine emulator and virtualizer. When using KVM, QEMU can virtualize x86, server and embedded PowerPC, 64-bit POWER, S390, 32-bit and 64-bit ARM, and MIPS guests.
entry.line: - [QEMU](https://www.qemu.org/) - QEMU is a generic and open source machine emulator and virtualizer. When using KVM, QEMU can virtualize x86, server and embedded PowerPC, 64-bit POWER, S390, 32-bit and 64-bit ARM, and MIPS guests.

evidence.observation: Tagline: "A generic and open source machine emulator and virtualizer". Features: full-system emulation, user-mode emulation, and "Run KVM and Xen virtual machines with near native performance". The latest release is 11.1.3 (Oct 28, 2026).
Under Host Architectures: "32-bit MIPS (removed in 10.2)", "64-bit MIPS (removed in 11.1)" and "32-bit PPC (removed in 10.2)". Also: "KVM guest support on 32-bit Arm hosts (removed in 5.2)".
The Supported Accelerators table lists KVM on Linux for "Arm, MIPS, PPC, RISC-V, s390x, x86". MIPS is still listed there, which conflicts with the removed-features page.

limitations: The QEMU intro page's accelerator table still lists MIPS for KVM, which looks like stale docs. The proposed wording avoids the architecture list either way.
I did not run QEMU.
assessment.newDescription: QEMU is a generic and open source machine emulator and virtualizer, providing full-system emulation and near-native virtualization with KVM and Xen.
assessment.reason: QEMU is still a generic, open source machine emulator and virtualizer, but the description's fixed KVM guest list is out of date. QEMU's official removed-features page shows 64-bit MIPS hosts removed in 11.1 and 32-bit MIPS in 10.2, which ends MIPS KVM guests in current releases. KVM on 32-bit Arm hosts was removed in 5.2. The current accelerator table also adds RISC-V. Durable wording taken from the homepage avoids this volatile architecture list.

entry.description: Cisco WAE, formerly known as Cariden MATE, provides a multi-vendor network simulation that enables capacity planning and what-if scenario analysis for carrier networks.
entry.line: - [Cisco WAN Automation Engine](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/routers/wae-planning/index.html) - Cisco WAE, formerly known as Cariden MATE, provides a multi-vendor network simulation that enables capacity planning and what-if scenario analysis for carrier networks.

evidence.observation: The EOL notice gives End-of-Sale November 15, 2026 and Last Date of Support May 31, 2028. All WAE versions, including 7.6 and MATE, are affected. It recommends migrating to Cisco Crosswork Planning and links its datasheet.
The page still describes WAE modeling, simulating and analyzing failures and what-if and capacity planning, and links to the EOL notices listing. It returns 403 to curl but was readable via WebFetch.

limitations: WAE remains supported until May 31, 2028, so the maintainer could keep the entry until then. Its end-of-sale is days away (Nov 15, 2026).
I did not confirm that Crosswork Planning is multi-vendor, so the proposed description omits that claim.
I read the datasheet details through search excerpts rather than a full page read.
assessment.newDescription: Cisco Crosswork Planning, the successor to Cisco WAE (formerly Cariden MATE), provides network modeling and simulation for capacity planning, failure and what-if scenario analysis.
assessment.reason: Cisco has issued an End-of-Sale/End-of-Life announcement covering all Cisco WAN Automation Engine versions, including WAE 7.6 and MATE products. The last order date is November 15, 2026 and the last date of support is May 31, 2028. The notice names Cisco Crosswork Planning as the migration product, 'our next-generation network planning and optimization platform ... that surpass[es] the sunsetting Cisco WAE'. Crosswork Planning provides network modeling, simulation, failure and what-if analysis, and capacity planning. The listed WAE page still loads via WebFetch (curl gets 403 from Akamai), so this is an officially documented successor, not a dead link.

entry.name: Cisco NSO
entry.description: NSO (former Tail-f NCS) is a multi-vendor automation and orchestration platform for physical and virtual networks for over 80+ vendors. NSO provides YANG-based programmability through a wide variety of interfaces including CLI, RESTCONF, NETCONF, Java, Python and web UI.
entry.line: - [Cisco NSO](https://cisco.com/go/nso) - NSO (former Tail-f NCS) is a multi-vendor automation and orchestration platform for physical and virtual networks for over 80+ vendors. NSO provides YANG-based programmability through a wide variety of interfaces including CLI, RESTCONF, NETCONF, Java, Python and web UI.

evidence.observation: 'NSO uses YANG as the overall modeling language to manage devices and services.' 'human interfaces like web UI and a CLI, programmable interfaces including RESTCONF, NETCONF, JSON-RPC, and language bindings including Java, Python, and Erlang.' It calls the product 'Cisco Crosswork Network Services Orchestrator (NSO) enabled by Tail-f' and gives no vendor count.
Official DevNet NSO documentation page is live (HTTP 200).
Redirects to www.cisco.com/go/nso, which returns HTTP 403 to curl. This looks like Cisco's bot filtering.

limitations: The 1,000+ third-party device types figure comes from a search snippet of the Cisco NED datasheet. I did not read it directly, so the proposed wording avoids any count.
I did not change the URL. cisco.com/go/nso is Cisco's own short link and likely works in browsers.
assessment.newDescription: NSO (Cisco Crosswork Network Services Orchestrator, formerly Tail-f NCS) is a multi-vendor automation and orchestration platform for physical and virtual networks. NSO provides YANG-based programmability through a wide variety of interfaces including CLI, RESTCONF, NETCONF, JSON-RPC, Java, Python and web UI.
assessment.reason: cisco.com/go/nso returns HTTP 403 to automated clients (bot blocking, not a dead link). The official NSO docs confirm the rest of the entry: Tail-f heritage ('enabled by Tail-f', 'ncs' naming), YANG-based multi-vendor device management, and northbound CLI, web UI, RESTCONF, NETCONF, JSON-RPC, and Java/Python/Erlang bindings. The '80+ vendors' count isn't stated in the current docs. Cisco now cites support for 1,000+ third-party device types via NEDs (search snippet), so the volatile count should be dropped. The product is now formally named Cisco Crosswork Network Services Orchestrator.

NetQ delivers actionable insights and operational intelligence about the health of your data center — from the container, virtual machine, or host, all the way to the switch and port, enabling a NetDevOps approach.

evidence.observation: Redirects (1 hop) to https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/ethernet-switching/netq/ with HTTP 200.

Page says: 'NVIDIA NetQ™ is a highly scalable network operations toolset that provides visibility, troubleshooting, correlation, and validation of your NVIDIA NVLink™ Switches and NVIDIA® Cumulus® fabrics in real time.' It also says 'NetQ uses agents on the switches and hosts to collect telemetry data' and mentions 'full continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) functionality' and 'Preventive Validation'.
Current docs title: 'NVIDIA NetQ 5.3 User Guide | Cumulus NetQ 5.3'.
Kubernetes/container monitoring page exists in the NetQ 4.10 guide (HTTP 200). The same path returns 404 for 4.15, 5.0, 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3.

limitations: A missing docs page is strong but not conclusive evidence that container monitoring was removed. I found no release note that explicitly removes it.
I did not run NetQ.
assessment.newDescription: NVIDIA NetQ (formerly Cumulus NetQ) is a scalable network operations toolset that uses switch and host agents and streaming telemetry to provide real-time visibility, troubleshooting and validation of NVIDIA Cumulus and NVLink fabrics, enabling a NetDevOps approach.
assessment.reason: The product is still relevant, but its identity has changed. The old cumulusnetworks.com URL 301-redirects to NVIDIA's NetQ page, and the vendor now calls the product "NVIDIA NetQ" ("Cumulus NetQ" survives only in the page title and docs path). NVIDIA describes it as a highly scalable network operations toolset that uses switch and host agents and telemetry for visibility, troubleshooting, correlation and validation. That still fits network automation (validation, telemetry, CI/CD-style operations). The listed claim of visibility "from the container, virtual machine" is no longer supported by current docs: the container-monitoring page exists in the NetQ 4.10 guide but returns 404 in 4.15 and 5.0 through 5.3. I recommend a rename, the canonical URL, and a description that leaves out the container/VM claim.

entry.name: Cisco Viptela
entry.description: Viptela provides Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) technology that allows global companies to build cost-effective WANs.
entry.line: - [Cisco Viptela](http://viptela.com/) - Viptela provides Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) technology that allows global companies to build cost-effective WANs.

evidence.observation: Proxy returns 502. DNS via dns.google: viptela.com has NOERROR with no A answer (SOA only), and www.viptela.com is NXDOMAIN (Status 3).

'To achieve simplification and consistency, the Cisco SD-WAN solution has been rebranded as Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN.' Lists vManage → Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, vSmart → Controller, vBond → Validator.
Read via WebFetch (curl got HTTP 403): Cisco SD-WAN product page, 'Automate provisioning and management in a single dashboard...'.
HTTP 200: 'Introduction - Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API, Release 26.2 - Cisco DevNet'.

limitations: Cisco's marketing page blocks curl (403) but was readable via WebFetch. Maintainers may prefer the DevNet API docs URL for a more automation-oriented link.
'Formerly Viptela' is attested on the Cisco Community forum and by third parties. Cisco's release notes confirm the Cisco SD-WAN → Catalyst SD-WAN rename.
assessment.newDescription: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (formerly Viptela) is Cisco's software-defined WAN solution, with centralized, automated provisioning and management through SD-WAN Manager and its APIs.
assessment.reason: viptela.com no longer resolves: Google DNS returns no A record for viptela.com and NXDOMAIN for www.viptela.com. Cisco acquired Viptela, and Cisco's own release notes state that 'the Cisco SD-WAN solution has been rebranded as Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN', with vManage renamed to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. This is the same product line under its official current name, not a competitor. Cisco's current SD-WAN page emphasizes automated provisioning and management, and DevNet documents the SD-WAN Manager API, which supports the network-automation fit. I recommend a rename with the Cisco URL.

entry.name: Infoblox Perl API
entry.description: - [Infoblox Perl API](https://demogm1.infoblox.com/api/doc/) and [Infoblox REST API](https://demogm1.infoblox.com/wapidoc/)
entry.line: - [Infoblox Perl API](https://demogm1.infoblox.com/api/doc/) and [Infoblox REST API](https://demogm1.infoblox.com/wapidoc/)

blockers: No official notice explicitly retires demogm1.infoblox.com. Its absence is inferred from NXDOMAIN and missing archives.

The successor link is a maintainer choice: the versioned WAPI PDF reference guide or the docs.infoblox.com 'Using NIOS APIs' page. A public appliance-hosted /wapidoc mirror (e.g. a university's) is not an Infoblox-owned destination.

evidence.observation: Status 3 (NXDOMAIN), with an SOA authority from the infoblox.com zone. Google DNS (https://dns.google/resolve?name=demogm1.infoblox.com&type=A) also returns Status 3.
Empty result: no archived captures for /wapidoc/ or /api/doc/.

'The Perl API (PAPI) for NIOS has been deprecated from NIOS 8.3 onwards. Infoblox recommends that you migrate to WAPI' and 'All enhancements and fixes for NIOS APIs are provided through WAPI from NIOS 8.4 onwards.' Detailed API info is in a PDF on docs.infoblox.com.

The official NIOS 9.0 documentation space is reachable (200). A web search surfaced the 'Infoblox NIOS WAPI 9.x Reference Guide' PDF under docs.infoblox.com/download/attachments/15433773/, which I did not open.

limitations: The DNS lookups went through public DoH resolvers, not Infoblox's authoritative servers. The host could exist on internal or split-horizon DNS.
The entry is a non-editable compound line, so no patch fields are supplied.
assessment.reason: Both linked hosts appear to be gone. demogm1.infoblox.com returns NXDOMAIN from Cloudflare and Google DNS-over-HTTPS (the infoblox.com zone answers authoritatively), the sandbox proxy returned 502, and the Wayback CDX has no captures. That points to a decommissioned demo Grid Master, not a transient failure, but DNS absence is still access evidence rather than an official statement. Infoblox officially says the Perl API (PAPI) has been deprecated since NIOS 8.3 and that WAPI is the supported REST API. WAPI docs are published as a PDF on docs.infoblox.com, plus each appliance's /wapidoc. The compound line is non-editable, so the maintainer must choose new destinations: probably drop the Perl API link and point the REST link at the official WAPI reference.

blockers: Whether O'Reilly still offers the ebook for free at the redirect target is unverified.
Whether the Cloudflare download page counts as an acceptable official replacement link (it is the authors' former employer and sponsor, and is gated by a lead form) needs a maintainer decision.

evidence.observation: curl followed redirects to https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/~/9781491992524, which returned 403. I saw no evidence of a free-download landing page remaining at O'Reilly.
Live page titled 'Free eBook: Network Automation at Scale | Cloudflare'. It describes the Ulinic/House book on Salt, NAPALM and Jinja/YAML and has a download form.
A search result shows the book's chapters ('The Salt Event Bus') in O'Reilly's library under the ISBN path.

limitations: O'Reilly blocks automated fetches, so I could not see the redirect target's content.
assessment.reason: The listed O'Reilly '.csp' free-ebook URL now redirects to the O'Reilly library page (ISBN 9781491992524), which returned 403 to automated clients. I could not confirm whether the book is still free from O'Reilly. Library pages are normally subscription-gated, so the 'free ebook from O'Reilly' claim may be outdated. Cloudflare hosts a page offering the same book as a free download behind a form. The book's content (Salt-based network automation by Ulinic and House) is still relevant.

Not stopping at network devices, but orchestrate end-to-end including firewalls, DDI (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) and other 3rd party tooling. Deploy your networks as Designed.
entry.line: - [NetYCE](https://netyce.com/) NetYCE lets you be in control of any and all of your networks, using its unique Design Driven Networking approach. Not stopping at network devices, but orchestrate end-to-end including firewalls, DDI (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) and other 3rd party tooling. Deploy your networks as Designed.

blockers: No official evidence that Netpicker is the documented successor to the NetYCE product, or that NetYCE is discontinued.
The entry is marked non-editable because the line is malformed.

evidence.observation: Redirects (1 hop) to https://netpicker.io/.

Netpicker describes itself as network testing: 'Continuously validate real network state before and after changes. Test configs, compliance, security, and network behavior. Automate remediation.' It is built on Python and pytest, supports 180+ vendors, and makes no mention of NetYCE or Design Driven Networking on the homepage.
Search result shows a NetYCE software-update knowledge-base article on Netpicker's support portal, which suggests NetYCE is still supported. I did not read it directly.

limitations: A Packet Pushers podcast (NAN087) reportedly says the NetYCE founders started Netpicker as a new modular product. That is secondary and not an official successor notice.
assessment.reason: netyce.com now redirects to netpicker.io. Netpicker is a separate network testing, compliance and automation product from the same team, now under the Flock9 brand. I found no official statement that the NetYCE 'Design Driven Networking' product was renamed, discontinued or succeeded by Netpicker. Netpicker's support site still hosts NetYCE knowledge-base articles. This entry is also not editable (malformed line with the link duplicated inside the description), so any change needs manual handling.

blockers: No official public end-of-sale/end-of-life statement was found for Talari SD-WAN.

evidence.observation: Redirects (2 hops) to https://www.oracle.com/communications/, a generic page with no Talari product content.
HTTP 200 'Oracle Talari Platforms - Home', describing Talari SD-WAN appliances (physical, virtual, cloud). Metadata: datePublished 2019-11-01, dateModified 2022-05-20.

Oracle's Talari Platforms documentation is still online, but it was last modified in May 2022. Third-party sources say the product is discontinued, but I found no public official end-of-life notice. Oracle's support-policy document does carry Talari-specific hardware support terms. Fit is also borderline: this is an SD-WAN product, and its network-automation value is not evident from the remaining sources. The maintainer should decide whether to point the entry at the docs page or drop it. I can't confirm removal from official evidence.
